requirements.statement: trade-imports-stub's address lookup simulator answers GET /simulator/address-lookup/v2.1/addresses with optional postcode or find (postcode winning when both are sent), a 400 'Either postcode or find is required' when neither is sent, and exactly and case-sensitively matched reserved terms: SW1A 1AA, 'Buckingham Palace' and 'Downing Street' give the three London fixtures shaped as the real gateway's dev response; ZZ1 1ZZ a 204; QQ1 1QQ a 400; XX1 1XX a 503; YY1 1YY an HTML 200; TT1 1TT the three fixtures after 15 seconds; anything else a 200 with no results. Before any of that it checks the bearer's scheme, RSA signature, api:// audience and expiry only, and answers a failed check with the gateway's exact 401 body and no WWW-Authenticate header.
requirements.why: It stands in for the address lookup on the local stack and will answer the address search once the search is built; nothing in the design changes it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-stub-p1-001 to p1-037 describe the simulator as built, and the tests in repo-stub-p1-040 to p1-053 prove it.

requirements.statement: Adding an address from the consignee, importer or place of destination address section, and adding an address in the address book, starts with a find-address step: the trader enters a UK postcode, picks the address from those found there, and lands on the address form filled from it. The place of origin, consignor, county parish holding and permanent address sections have no find-address step.
requirements.why: The design starts these add-address journeys with a postcode search. Only the receiving roles get it because the address book refuses a consignee, importer or place of destination outside the United Kingdom, while a place of origin or consignor may be abroad, so a UK postcode search fits only the former. The germinal products copy of these sections takes the same step, and plants takes it in the same increment for any of these sections it has.

conflicts.about: Which address sections get the find-address step, where the prototype's answer comes from its app/data files.

positions.says: The consignee, importer and place of destination sections get the find-address pages, because its app/data use-group file maps them to 'destination-and-receiver'.
A rule claim from the prototype's app/data files is refused as readily as a data one.
The address book refuses a consignee, importer or place of destination outside the United Kingdom.

conflicts.outcome: The rulings win: the app/data rule is set aside, and the sections that get a UK postcode search are chosen by the address book's own rule that consignee, importer and place of destination must be in the United Kingdom, while place of origin and consignor may be abroad. The same three sections result, on the real model's ground (req-address-lookup-001).

conflicts.about: Whether the add-address journeys start with the postcode find-address step now, as the design shows.

positions.says: Each destination-and-receiver section and the address book's add journey start with a find-address page.
Address search is not to be built yet: it is concept work, not deadline work.
Address search is blocked until the address lookup becomes a real feature.

conflicts.outcome: The rulings win on timing: the find-address pages are adopted as designed but blocked, parked as concept work and waiting on the INS address lookup becoming a real feature, and re-distilled once it lands. Until then every add-address page offers manual entry only (req-1830, req-1862). Nothing is overruled: the prototype's design still backs the blocked requirements.
